DI BAGONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. S. 2021 Krizshelle Carandang ishelcarandanq.ph@gmail.com Barangay VII-E (Pob.), San Pablo city, Laguna 0977 272 5365 Dear Ms. Carandang: This has reference to your email-inquiry dated 4 March 2024, coursed through the Presidential Action Center, relative to the procedure of barangay hearing in Barangay 3, Alaminos, Laguna. You seek clarification based on the following circumstances: "Nais kong magtanong sa ahensya tungkol sa barangay hearing procedure. May isang barangay sa Alaminos, Laguna ang hindi kami binigyan ng official summon at hinayaan lang rin nila na hindi mag-attend ang nirereklamo naming isang residente nila. Sa unang hearing pa lang ay hindi na nag-attend iyong tao at ang sabi ng barangay lupon ay hindi raw puwedeng pilitin. Gusto ko lang malaman kung tama ba ang procedure ng hearing sa Barangay 3, Alaminos, Laguna at kung sakali naman na mapatunayan na hindi tama ang procedure ng barangay official ay ano ang maaring maging sanction nila?" Hence, your request for guidance as to whether proper implementation of the law was done and the possible actions that may be taken against the concerned erring public officials, if any. Before we discuss in detail, we cite as reference the pertinent provision provided under the Local Government Code with regard to the procedure for amicable settlement, to wit: SECTION 410. Procedure for Amicable Settlement. — (a) Who may initiate proceeding - Upon payment of the appropriate filing fee, any individual who has a cause of action against another individual involving any matter within the authority of the lupon may complain, orally or in writing, to the lupon chairman of the Barangay. (b) Mediation by lupon chairman - Upon receipt of the complaint, the lupon chairman shall within the next working day summon the respondent(s), with notice to the complainant(s) for them and their witnesses to appear before him for a mediation of their conflicting interests. If he fails in his mediation effort within fifteen (15) days from the first meeting of the parties before him, he shall forthwith set a date for the constitution of the pangkat in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. (c) Suspension of prescriptive period of offenses - While the dispute is under mediation, conciliation, or arbitration, the prescriptive periods for offenses and cause of action under existing laws shall be interrupted upon filing of the complaint with the Punong Barangay. The prescriptive periods shall resume "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

upon receipt by the complainant of the complaint or the certificate of repudiation or of the certification to file action issued by the lupon or pangkat secretary: Provided, however, that such interruption shall not exceed sixty (60) days from the filing of the complaint with the Punong Barangay. (d) Issuance of summons; hearing; grounds for disqualification- The pangkat shall convene not later than three (3) days from its constitution, on the day and hour set by the lupon chairman, to hear both parties and their witnesses, simplify issues, and explore all possibilities for amicable settlement. For this purpose, the pangkat may issue summons for the personal appearance of parties and witnesses before it. In the event that a party moves to disqualify any member of the pangkat by reason of relationship, bias, interest, or any other similar grounds discovered after the constitution of the pangkat, the matter shall be resolved by the affirmative vote of the majority of the pangkat whose decision shall be final. Should disqualification be decided upon, the resulting vacancy shall be filled as herein provided for. (e) Period to arrive at a settlement - The pangkat shall arrive at a settlement or resolution of the dispute within fifteen (15) days from the day it convenes in accordance with this section. This period shall, at the discretion of the pangkat, be extendible for another period which shall not exceed fifteen (15) days, except in clearly meritorious cases. On the other hand, the implementing rules and regulations of the Katarungang Pambarangay Law provides for the following instances in case of refusal or failure of any parties or witness to appear before the lupon or pagkat. SEC. 515. REFUSAL OR FAILURE OF ANY PARTY OR WITNESS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE LUPON OR PANGKAT.- Refusal or willful failure of any party or witness to appear before the !upon or pangkat in compliance with a summons issued pursuant to the provisions on the Katarungang Pambarangay under Chapter 7, Title One of Book Ill of this Code may be punished by the city or municipal court as for indirect contempt of court upon application filed therewith by the !upon chairman, the pangkat chairman, or by any of the contending parties. Such refusal or willful failure to appear, shall be reflected in the records of the lupon secretary or in the minutes of the pangkat secretary and shall bar the complainant who fails to appear, from seeking judicial• recourse for the same cause of action, and the respondent who refuses to appear from filing any counterclaim arising out of, or necessarily connected with the complainti. As aptly put, the failure of the complainant to appear without justifiable cause, will cause the dismissal of his/her complaint and may be barred from filing a case in court. In case of refusal or willful failure of the respondent to appear in obedience to the summons, the latter may be barred from filing any counterclaim arising from the said complaint. It is important to note that summons must be properly and timely issued within three (3) days after the payment of the filing fee by the complainant. Proper and timely service of summons is essential for the barangay hearing process. Both parties should be officially notified of the hearing through a Notice of Hearing and Summon. The IRR of the Katarungang Pambarangay law does not provide that at least three (3) hearing dates must be assigned for a resolution of a case. On the contrary, the law only THE REVISED KATARUNGANG PAMBARANGAY LAW (Sections 399-422, Chapter 7) Title one, Book II and Section 515, Book IV, Title I of RA 7160. Page 2 of 3

provides that the lupon shall arrive at a settlement or resolution of the dispute within fifteen (15) days from the day it convenes. Further, in all cases where the respondent fails to appear at the mediation proceedings before the Punong Barangay, and the respondent's refusal or willful failure to appear is without justifiable cause after notice and hearing, the same shall be sufficient basis for the issuance of a Certification to File Action (CFA). This proves that the efforts to settle the dispute amicably following the procedures laid down under the Katarungang Pambarangay Law failed and the parties may now escalate the settlement of said dispute with the proper courts. In resolving your inquiry, we agree that while the barangay cannot insist or compel the attendance of the other party, their consequent absence without justification has its legal repercussions as already discussed. Lastly, an elective local official may be disciplined, suspended or removed from office in case of misconduct in office, gross negligence or dereliction of duty2 as provided under the Local Government Code. Finally, this opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, it is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you very much.
